summary: LocalSetup 4.90.1 includes the reviewed Herdr retirement and terminal startup changes since the last published release, together with a correction to SDK wheel helper permissions and the reviewed dependency maintenance.

highlights.text: Retire only an explicitly selected uninitialized Herdr creation: the shared owner requires the original request and creation token, exact pane and stable terminal identities, discard acknowledgement, and fresh evidence that no operation, writer or descendant work occupies the current shell.

Preserve original owner and reservation bytes before closing, durably fence the close before dispatch, and reconcile a lost response without repeating it. Both original native identifiers must be conclusively absent before a later ordinary allocation for that same binding is permitted; recovery never automatically creates a replacement or runs a workload.

Keep caller-owned storage in place. Optional retirement requires an exact bounded snapshot, durable writes and a nonblocking cross-process lock. Raw custom-store lock contention is reported as pane_busy before dispatch, while operation-body and cleanup failures are not reclassified as harmless lock refusal.

Preserve the controlled Herdr startup loader across login-profile changes, recover a missing prior generation only from completed-operation and native-absence proof, and translate the child fraction to Herdr's parent-oriented split ratio.

Carry forward the reviewed dependency graph, hash-pinned SDK and storage exports, reviewed routing-catalog evidence and bounded native qualification diagnostics from the unpublished maintenance line. Runtime, build and optional storage scopes remain separate; client model configuration is unchanged.

Correct SDK wheel helper permissions: BuildSDK sets the packaged sudo_askpass helper to mode 0755 without changing its bytes and rejects symlinked helper destinations. Installed runtime protection still rejects a non-executable or group- or world-writable helper.

compatibility: The optional recovery methods extend managed-terminal API version 1. Existing callers that do not request retirement retain their normal lifecycle, and older runtimes must refuse the missing optional capability rather than substitute generic cleanup.

The new retirement process proof requires Linux /proc visibility and provable native server ancestry. Missing platform, identity or occupancy evidence refuses recovery; normal Herdr and tmux operation support is unchanged.

Keep the original retirement ID and durable evidence until reconciliation and any subsequent allocation complete. Do not delete journals, replay a close or downgrade the recovery owner to bypass an unknown outcome.

Safe wheel permission metadata does not make an arbitrary installer secure: installation permissions also depend on the installer and its environment. The installed qualification used the existing protected contract: a private cache, filtered environment, --no-config, --offline, --link-mode copy and umask 077.

Dependency and routing-catalog reviews are point-in-time evidence, not a package-safety or per-account model-access guarantee. This release does not authorize changes to configured models, schedules or host services.
update: Use the existing verified installation or source-refresh procedure, and verify the released archive and its checksum/SBOM sidecars. Managed consumers retain their last qualified pin until the new release passes their compatibility checks.

Retirement is an explicitly authorized discard of one exact owned local shell, including its unsubmitted input and shell-local state. Ordinary cleanup and command dispatch do not grant that authority.
verification: The corrected installed-wheel regression passed, as did 25 SDK build and payload tests and 25 FleetOps adapter tests against the corrected installed wheel, including the previously failing tmux subcases.

The earlier shared recovery and acquisition-boundary changes passed independent source review and 34 focused lifecycle and real-PTY tests. The PTY fixtures reported three fork-related deprecation warnings under the threaded test runner.

An earlier registered-CLI retirement smoke used the real FleetOps store and shared service to verify exact original archives, one close, idempotency, lost-response reconciliation and structured held-lock refusal. Native I/O and process identity were simulated; this is not live-host qualification.

Release activation requires full validation and all required release gates for the exact final candidate. The earlier 4.90.0 candidate archive is not the corrected deliverable. Focused results do not establish provider completion or health, live-host readiness, or acceptance of a final published artifact.
Verify the exact framework archive with its .sha256 checksum and .cdx.json SBOM sidecars before adopting it.
